_comment: Curated bibliographies for every author in the fork owner's library (S:\My Books).
Compiled from web sources - publisher pages, author sites, Wikipedia, ISFDB - and NOT from
Open Library. That is deliberate: Open Library is the source under test, so deriving ground
truth from it would make BibliographyAccuracyFixture circular and unable to detect its errors.
Open Library was consulted only afterwards, to cross-check for omissions, and the disagreements
Scope follows the precedent the owner set with Frank Herbert: an author's own primary books.
Included:  novels, and for non-fiction authors their principal authored books; co-authored works
Excluded:  omnibuses and box sets, anthologies the author contributed a story to, volumes they
only edited, translations, graphic-novel adaptations of their own work, and posthumous
'confidence' is honest about how much this list should be trusted:
high   - well-documented author, bibliography corroborated by multiple independent sources.
medium - corroborated, but the author is obscure or prolific enough that omissions are likely.
low    - thin sourcing. Verify before relying on it.
Only the three authors in expected_bibliographies.json are wired into the accuracy fixture.
Promoting one from here needs its Open Library payload fetched (see refresh-corpus.sh) and its
author key confirmed - see the warnings below, several keys are wrong or conflated.

authors.name: Annalee Newitz

titles.title: Pretend We're Dead: Capitalist Monsters in American Pop Culture
Four Lost Cities: A Secret History of the Urban Age
Stories Are Weapons: Psychological Warfare and the American Mind

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. 'She's Such a Geek' is an anthology Newitz co-edited, excluded by scope.

authors.name: Apostolos Doxiadis

titles.title: Logicomix: An Epic Search for Truth

authors.openLibraryNotes: WRONG KEY BY DEFAULT. Author search for 'Apostolos Doxiadis' returns OL10836046A, a different person with 3 works ('Greek Commander'). The real author is OL87267A, filed as 'Apostolos K. Doxiadēs'. Readarr's author search would add the wrong one.

authors.name: Brené Brown

titles.title: I Thought It Was Just Me (But It Isn't)

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Sources count 17 'books' including workbooks, curricula and audio-only titles; only the principal authored books are listed. 'The Art of Asking' and 'You Are Your Best Thing' are not hers alone - the latter she co-edited with Tarana Burke.

authors.name: Charles H. Kahn

titles.title: Anaximander and the Origins of Greek Cosmology
The Art and Thought of Heraclitus
Pythagoras and the Pythagoreans: A Brief History

authors.openLibraryNotes: CONFLATED KEY. OL455933A mixes this Charles H. Kahn (1928-2023, classicist at Penn) with an unrelated author of 'Personal deductions in the federal income tax', 'Employee compensation under the income tax' and 'Going places with your personality'. Four of the fourteen English works under that key are not his.

authors.name: Clark R. Mollenhoff

titles.title: Tentacles of Power: The Story of Jimmy Hoffa
The Pentagon: Politics, Profits and Plunder
Strike Force: Organized Crime and the Government
The President Who Failed: Carter Out of Control
Atanasoff: Forgotten Father of the Computer
Ballad to an Iowa Farmer and Other Reflections

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Sources describe him as 'author of eleven previous books' at the time of Atanasoff, which matches this list. 'Life Line of Democracy' (1964) appears in Open Library and may be a pamphlet rather than a book - unverified.

authors.name: David Howard-Pitney

titles.title: The Afro-American Jeremiad: Appeals for Justice in America
Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X, and the Civil Rights Struggle of the 1950s and 1960s
The African American Jeremiad: Appeals for Justice in America
titles.note: revised edition of the 1990 book; arguably the same work

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct but most of its 16 English works are Bedford/St. Martin's course-pack bundles ('American Promise 3e V2 & Reading the American Past 3e V2 & ...'), not distinct books. This author is a good stress test for the non-book filter.

authors.name: Eoin Colfer

titles.title: The Legend of Captain Crow's Teeth
The Legend of the Worst Boy in the World
The Fowl Twins Deny All Charges
The Fowl Twins Get What They Deserve

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct and unusually well populated (93 editions on Artemis Fowl). Picture books and the 'Illegal'/'Imaginary Fred' illustrated collaborations are omitted; add them if children's picture books should count. The library folder holds 'Artemis Begins', which is not an official Colfer title - likely a renamed omnibus.

authors.name: Frank Herbert
authors.openLibraryNotes: Full list lives in expected_bibliographies.json - this author is wired into the accuracy fixture.

authors.name: Brian Herbert
authors.openLibraryNotes: Full list lives in expected_bibliographies.json - this author is wired into the accuracy fixture.

authors.name: Gareth Brown
authors.openLibraryNotes: CONFLATED KEY. OL2779405A holds both this Gareth Brown (Scottish novelist, NHS Scotland) and an unrelated one who writes about scooter culture - 'Scooter Boys' (1996), 'Mods and Rockers' (2022), plus 'Short Fat Chick to Marathon Runner'. Four of six English works under the key are not his.

authors.name: J. K. Rowling

titles.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Two scope calls worth revisiting: the Cormoran Strike novels are published as Robert Galbraith and are excluded here as a separate authorial identity, and the Hogwarts Library companions (Fantastic Beasts, Quidditch Through the Ages, Tales of Beedle the Bard) are excluded as companion volumes. Open Library files all of them under this key.

authors.name: J. R. R. Tolkien
authors.openLibraryNotes: SCOPE CALL, flag for review. Applying the Frank Herbert precedent - no posthumous assemblies - excludes The Silmarillion, Unfinished Tales, The Children of Hurin, Beren and Luthien, The Fall of Gondolin and all twelve History of Middle-earth volumes, all edited by Christopher Tolkien after 1973. That is defensible but leaves only the eight works published in Tolkien's lifetime, and most readers would expect The Silmarillion. Open Library lists 204 English works under this key.

authors.name: John Steinbeck

titles.title: The Short Reign of Pippin IV

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Novels only. His non-fiction (Sea of Cortez, A Russian Journal, Travels with Charley, America and Americans, Once There Was a War) and the story collection The Long Valley are excluded by scope, as is the posthumous Acts of King Arthur. Open Library dates two works to 1611 and 1695, which is a good calendar-corruption test case.

authors.name: Lev Grossman
authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. 'Dangerous Women', 'Unfettered' and 'Other Worlds Than These' are anthologies he contributed to; Open Library files them under this key and they should be filtered as such.

authors.name: Matt Dinniman

titles.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
The Eye of the Bedlam Bride

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Sources disagree about The Shivered Sky: Open Library has it as a single 2003 book, one reading-order site splits it into a three-book series (Every Grain of Sand / In the City of Demons / The Great Devouring Darkness). Listed as one book, unverified. Open Library also shows a 2026 'Traps and Specters' not corroborated elsewhere.

authors.name: Oscar Ratti

titles.title: Secrets of the Samurai: The Martial Arts of Feudal Japan

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. Ratti was primarily the illustrator on both, Westbrook the writer, but both are credited as authors throughout. 'The Medieval Health Handbook' and 'Tales of the Hermit' appear under the key and are unverified as his own books.

authors.name: Sidney Sheldon

titles.title: Are You Afraid of the Dark?

authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. The 18 novels; his memoir The Other Side of Me (2005) is excluded by scope, as are the posthumous 'Sidney Sheldon's ...' continuations written by Tilly Bagshawe, which Open Library files under this key. Open Library dates Master of the Game to 1905.

authors.name: Sophia Turner
authors.openLibraryNotes: NOT IN OPEN LIBRARY. A direct title search for 'Machines of Consent' returns nothing related. The author-name search resolves to OL3716471A, an unrelated Sophia Turner who wrote 'Devastating Truth' (2005). This book is unreachable from Open Library at any filter setting, and is the clearest single argument in this library for a second IBookMetadataProvider. Debut novel; the author is a New Zealand programming-language designer.

authors.name: Tim Berners-Lee
authors.openLibraryNotes: Key is correct. 'Spinning the Semantic Web' and 'A Framework for Web Science' are academic volumes he contributed to rather than authored, and 'The WWW Virtual Library' is not a book.
